Copied 03:16 Keiko Fujimori was sworn in as Peru’s first democratically elected female president, marking the return of one of the country’s most influential and divisive political dynasties. During her inauguration, she pledged to uphold the constitution and govern responsibly as she begins a five-year term. Supporters celebrated her victory, while protesters denounced her presidency, reflecting deep political divisions following her narrow election win. The ceremony was attended by several conservative Latin American leaders, underscoring a broader rightward shift in the region. Fujimori now faces the challenge of governing a polarized nation. excerpts:
President Dina Boluarte became Peru’s first woman president under the constitutional rules of succession. Boluarte, a Lima-based lawyer and civil servant originally from the south-central department of Apurímac, a Quechua-speaking region, had been elected on the Perú Libre party slate. However, she distanced herself from Castillo and the party once in office. Boluarte faced an immediate challenge to her authority from Castillo’s rural and Indigenous supporters, who considered the former president a champion of their rights.
